fact: STELLARIX Senegal (AXIAN Group) has expanded its Senegal data centre capacity to host businesses' workloads and cloud services; no date for the expansion is given, so the publication date 2026-10-02 is used.

Xalam Analytics estimates about 5 live commercial data centre facilities in Senegal in 2025 (commercial meaning space and power leased to third parties), with about 1.8 MW live critical IT load and about 75% occupancy by third-party customers; no facility is named.
Stellarix Senegal, part of Axian, operates a data centre at Diamniadio offering colocation, cloud, connectivity and cybersecurity to outside customers, including banks and financial institutions.
Stellarix Senegal's managing director states its Diamniadio data centre is Tier 3 (operator's statement, no certification named).

Xalam Analytics estimates that Senegal had about 5 live commercial data centre facilities leasing colocation space and power to third parties in 2024, with about 1.6MW of live critical IT load, about 60% occupied by third-party customers; no facility is named in the text and telco facilities held about 60% of capacity.

AIIM's release says N+ONE, a carrier-neutral data center owner and operator, has existing campuses in Senegal that it will expand; no facility is named and the date is the release's published month (August 2023, inferred).

Onix Data Centre says its carrier-neutral facility at the Almadies 2Africa cable landing station in Dakar launched on 16 February 2023, with the build still in progress and completion expected Q4 2023.
DatacenterDynamics reports Onix launched a neutral colocation data center at the 2Africa cable landing station in Dakar on 16 February 2023, per Onix's CEO.

Dakaractu reported on 21 June 2021 that the ADIE-run Diamniadio state data centre, built over three years with two computer rooms, was to be inaugurated on 22 June 2021, and that the private sector could also use its space.
ADIE's director general described the Diamniadio state data centre (operator ADIE) as a Tier 3 type infrastructure; this is the agency's own statement, with no certification named.

DatacenterDynamics reported on 7 July 2017 that a new Tier III data center built by SenConnect for Tigo, both Millicom subsidiaries, had opened in Diamniadio, with Uptime's EMEA head calling it suited to storing enterprise data.
The SenConnect/Tigo Diamniadio data center opened in July 2017 was Tier 3 Design certified by the Uptime Institute (design certification, not constructed facility).

The national Datacenter de Diamniadio, run by ADIE (now Senegal Numerique SA), was inaugurated and put into service on 22 June 2021, with a 250 m2 space reserved for the national and international private sector alongside one for the administration.
ADIE states that the Diamniadio national Datacenter, inaugurated 22 June 2021 and in service, is the state's first Tier 3 data centre (operator's own statement, no certifier named).

CIO Mag reports ADIE's national data centre at Diamniadio was inaugurated on 22 June 2021 by President Macky Sall, to host data of public administration and the private sector (1,000 TB storage, 99.982% availability).
CIO Mag describes the Diamniadio national data centre, built by ADIE with Huawei, as a Tier 3 type facility (a stated rating, no certifier named).
Financial Afrik reports Sonatel inaugurated its Dakar data centre on 20 June 2017 (2,224 m2 building, three 250 m2 server rooms), letting companies and administrations outsource their servers.
Financial Afrik states Sonatel's Dakar data centre is Tier 3+ (a stated rating, no certifier named).

Senegal Numerique SA (SENUM) states the Diamniadio National Datacenter, a hosting and storage facility that also reserves a technical room for SMEs, start-ups and the private sector, was inaugurated by President Macky Sall on 22 June 2021.
SENUM, the operator, states the Diamniadio National Datacenter is the first national Tier 3 datacenter (operator statement, no Uptime Institute certification cited); inaugurated 22 June 2021.

Data Landscapers states that Onix operates a Tier IV carrier-neutral data centre at the 2Africa landing in Dakar, Senegal, described as built, certified and selling capacity today (certification body not named); no opening date given, so the article's published date 2026-06-11 is used.
